name: The Survivalist
description: Greetings! I'm Quinn Collins, your Drop Supervisor and coincidental survival specialist. I've been instructed to help you get started in this technologically desolate world, starting from the ground up. Let's begin this journey towards kicking some ass!

quests.name: Iron Age, finally
quests.description: To actually get to use your newly acquired Iron, you will have to, you guessed it, make an iron anvil.

tasks.longDescription: Show me you have created the following item:

quests.name: Crucible
quests.description: The crucible allows you to make more efficient use of your charcoal forge by providing 9 additional slots to heat up items. It also does so slightly faster than the forge itself, though it also needs time to heat up. so it's best used for bulk melting. Its biggest advantage though is that it can be used to automatically melt, alloy and cast metal. molds and metal can be inserted from the side and top and the filled molds taken out from the bottom. the latter does pose an obvious issue though as that's usually where the forge is located, which has similar problems refueling it. If you wish to use it for more large-scale operations, look into options to transfer items into blocks using either entity-based logistics or link blocks wirelessly.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following item:

quests.name: Coke Oven
quests.description: I suspect that you are starting to hate how inefficient it is to just put your wood in a pile and light it on fire. Fortunately, i found an old Patent in our database with detailed instructions on how to build a "coke oven" using some graphite and caminite.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following items:

quests.name: Budget Slimeballs
quests.description: If you are having trouble locating slimes underground, you can use bone meal and limewater to make glue which works in basically the same way.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: Lamp Lighting
quests.description: By working any metal on an anvil, you can make some oil lamps. these are an upgrade to the torch as they still go out, but last much longer. The trade-off is that while torches can just be re-lit, these consume fuel, though the amount is negligible in most cases. If you want to use them long-term, consider making lamp posts out of pipes that keep them fueled with, for example, creosote from your coke ovens. Lamps cannot attach to many pipes, but a fluid extractor is a suitable "adapter"

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have created the following items:

quests.name: Farming 101
quests.description: To make sure your crops can grow, look at their tooltip whether the current temperature and humidity allows for it. You'll get best results when the temperature stays within acceptable bounds year-round. It takes pretty long to grow them though, and you may only get a couple harvests in before winter. Also, no randomTicks involved, so forget bone meal and co.

tasks.longDescription: A bit tedious at first, but definitely better than hunting meat forever.

quests.name: [i] Nutrition and Health
quests.description: The food here seems to be of rather poor quality compared to our nutrient replicator made meals. As a result, your health will be declining if you only consume one or a few types of nutrients. We've calculated that it'll take ~ 20 meals' time for your body to get a meal out of your system completely, so those 20 foods will contribute to your health significantly. Try to maximize their value by cooking meals like sandwiches, soups or salads. If you want to know how your nutrient levels are at the moment, we've implemented a low-tech blood scanning machine. the screen should be located on a tab right of your inventory. If you want to see your armor status and other HUD elements, go to Mod options -> terrafirmacraft -> client -> display and switch "Use Vanilla Health Bar" on.

quests.name: Basic Devices
quests.description: Now that you have your saw, you can use it to make lumber which can be made into planks, and finally a crafting table that fits your wood type of choice. I don't think i have to tell you how important this thing is.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made the following item:

quests.name: Akashic Tome
quests.description: You're starting to amass quite the stockpile of books. Fortunately, our Engineers got you covered, using about the level of problem solving you'd expect at that paygrade: Just bind it all together into a bigger book! The Akashic Tome is effectively just that. Simply craft it together with any book you want to deposit into it. right-click to select which one you want to look at. Left-click to return to the Index once your reading session is over.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have created this item:

quests.name: Welcome Back, I guess
quests.description: Death is, while not inevitable, likely to come for you while down there. fortunately we make frequent backups of your consciousness through your tablet and can send down clones to keep your knowledge intact. As it's your first time, I'll be able to refund you some reputation. Haven't had much luck with calming down the crew tho. By clicking "Claim Reward", you agree to try your best to not die again.

tasks.longDescription: You must have died 1 time to see this message

quests.name: Ceramics
quests.description: Due to some unfamiliar geology, it appears that clay is deposited in the dirt rather than at the bottom of rivers or swamps. to top it all off, literally, the local grass can grow on clay aswell, making it near-impossible to find. Fortunately, there are a few species of plant that Only grow on top of clay, so keep an eye out for those. For an illustrated list, please refer to the tfc manual. Once you find some clay, it's wise to just grab a rock shovel and dig it all up, if you can carry that much. then, knap it (needs at least 5 clay in your hand) and fire the result in a pit kiln.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following items:
Show me that you have obtained the following items:

quests.name: [i] efficient Plate forging
quests.description: I have devised a method to get plates more efficiently, requiring only one ingot istead of the initial two. However, it needs the anvil to be harder than the material you're trying to forge, so a Tier 2 metal like bronze can only be processed efficiently on a Tier 3 anvil like one made of wrought iron, and so on.

quests.name: Automating Latex Extraction
quests.description: The latex extractor is not without its quirks, so i figured i'd try and automate it myself so you don't have to stare at it for 5 hours while tearing your hair out. first off, on larger plantations, it may be advantageous to use an ender porcupine with 3 users, one for re-cutting the vein, one for grabbing filled bowls and one for placing the emptied ones. the speed at which it goes through its specified area is not an issue as the extraction takes so long anyway. You can then have a scanner only activate the extracting user if a bowl is already present.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following items:

quests.name: What is this thing?
quests.description: This handy device, not much more than a complex mechanical computer, can be used to keep in touch with us, the research team, and can be used to show us items you've gathered through very rudimentary composition sensors. It kinda started out as one of Carmile's side projects, laughed off for lack of use cases. Now we know better. Until they find out a way to make it also be able to send us items however, it won't be much more than a glorified guide book.

tasks.longDescription: To see if everything's working, why don't you scan a block of dirt?

quests.name: Moving liquids
quests.description: You thought this was going to take some exotic kinds of steel to get this, didn't you?

tasks.longDescription: Show me you have obtained this item:

quests.name: [i] Support beams
quests.description: Support beams are essential for any Miner not wanting their last words to be "LET'S GO GAMBLING!". Once you set them up to form a sort of upside-down U-shape, they will prevent ANY gravity-affected block, including gravel, dirt, and loose cobble, from falling aswell as preventing rock from caving in. It does this up to 7 blocks sideways and 3 blocks up and down.

quests.name: Hammer Time!
quests.description: Use your new mining tools to get some industrial amounts of copper, at least 14 ingots' worth for now. melt them down and cast them into ingots. then, use a hammer on some raw igneous rock to form it into a primitive anvil, and weld the copper into double ingots. Reheat over a forge or firepit if necessary. once you have 7 of them, assemble them into an anvil that is useful for more than just welding.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: The charcoal pit
quests.description: Charcoal will most likely be the first "real" fuel you have access to. as of now, with no access to high-quality fire bricks, its creation is simplistic, but inefficient. simply put down logs on the ground while sneaking to create a log pile. the more logs in the pile, the more charcoal you'll get. You can put as many of these piles adjacent to one another as you like, amounting to more coal per round. Then, seal it with some dirt and light the last exposed block on fire before covering that too. once the smoke is gone, it is safe to dig up.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following items:

quests.name: Leatherworking
quests.description: To refine those raw hides into genuine leather, you must first soak it in limewater, then play it onto a log and scrape it clean using a knife. make sure it's actually clean before picking it up, otherwise progress will be lost. then, wash it in some fresh water and finally tan it using tannin you get by soaking certain kinds of logs (mostly darkish ones) in fresh water.

tasks.longDescription: Please show me that you have obtained the following items:
Please show me that you have obtained the following items:

quests.name: To build a Fire
quests.description: Fire is essential in keeping your shelter lit up and cooking meat. To form it, make a firestarter and hold right-click on 3 sticks and one log that've been dropped onto the ground.

tasks.longDescription: You should probably make some torches pretty early on. these will go out after 3 days, but it's the best thing we've got right now.

quests.name: Bloomery
quests.description: The bloomery uses carbon monoxide to siphon the oxygen from iron-rich ore, leaving a bloom of elementary Iron and slag that can be pounded off. See the reference guide for how it's constructed.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have made this item:

quests.name: The Oven
quests.description: To make bread and fire some special kinds of ceramics, you will need an oven. To form it, you will need some oven chimneys, two oven walls, and one or more ovens themselves. For it to work, make sure that  1) Every oven is adjacent to either another oven or an oven wall on the left and right, 2) that any chimneys you place on top are at least 3 blocks tall, and 3) that any oven is at most two blocks away from a chimney (horizontally), so every chimney can support 5 ovens. To fire it, put some straw in all of the front slots and put two charcoal in the back of one of them, then light that one. The longer the oven is, the more fuel-efficient it's going to be as only those two pieces are required to power the entire thing, no matter how long.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you've made the following items:

quests.name: Rubber Trees
quests.description: Both the Hevea and Rubber Fig are capable of producing latex. to extract it, make sure that the tree is still alive, aka there's soil beneath it and at least some of its leaves are still there. we want this to be renewable, don't we? then, with a hammer in your other hand, place a wrought iron groove onto the side of one of its logs. Only one per tree is possible. then, put a bowl mount and an empty fluid bowl (just a ceramic pot placed in the crafting grid) onto the groove, henceforth refered to as the extractor. To begin extraction, click the extractor with any kind of knife. The Trees will randomly try to seal the wound, so it might be wise to set up mechanical users with knives pointing at the extractor.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have the necessary components for an extraction device:
Then, once you got some rubber-producing trees, show me that you have got some latex from them.

quests.name: "Parchment"
quests.description: By substituting the tannin in the last step with white dye fluid, you can bleach the hide and turn it into what amounts to paper. Liquid dye is made with white dye and hot spring water in a barrel.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained this item:

quests.name: Animal Husbandry
quests.description: When hunting, it may be wise to only go for the wild animals instead of the ones that can be domesticated, so creatures like pheasants, deer, rabbits, and, surprisingly, turkeys. Others, like cattle, sheep and chickens can be domesticated by using grain to feed them once every day. Once an animal is fully familiarized, it will show a border around its heart icon which means that it will not become defamiliarized again, while that risk is prevalent in earlier stages. if you feed two animals of opposite sex with maxxed out familiarity within the same day, they will breed. they don't just throw out children like crazy, though, and pregnancies and incubation times are something to be aware of. Milkable animals do not grow old.

tasks.longDescription: A small price to pay for dairy

quests.name: Basic Materials
quests.description: Knap yourself a couple of stone knives and axes for now to defend yourself, aswell as gather straw from tall grass and chop down some trees. Most natural materials are affected by gravity, so those are about the only things that can get you a shelter for the night. Both straw and logs are also essential for a pit kiln.                 I once again apologize for not being able to give you any starting tools. As you know, 99% of our equipment is electric and someone thought that the last remaining hacksaw would be the perfect tool for getting the replicator in the caffeteria back up and running. May they rest in peace.

tasks.longDescription: To make a pit kiln, place up to 4 items in a small hole in the ground by using the "V" key. then, cover it in 8 straw and 8 logs. you can put multiple of these diaginally and light them all at once. For now, show me that you have enough materials to make at least one.

quests.name: Actual Rubber!
quests.description: To make rubber, there are two ways. the first one is rather inefficient and we would only recommend it if you want to start out with replicating light industry machines listed in the "industrialcraft" category: simply get some plastic of any color and dunk it into some latex for a few hours, then smelting it, foregoing the vulcanization process at the cost of efficiency. If you want to squeeze evrrything out of your trees, and i bet you'd want to, because they produce latex at a stunningly slow pace, you'll need a coagulator and vulcanizer, non-negligible amounts of sulfur, vulcanization agents, a metal press, and last but not least formic acid all combined in one production line. this method does yield way more for the effort, however.

tasks.longDescription: Show me that you have obtained the following item:

quests.name: [i] Seasons and the callendar
quests.description: We've identified that this planet has a bit of an axial tilt. We predict that this could lead to long-term fluctuations in sunlight exposure and thus different weather, even going so far as having periods where water will solidify. This might prove rather bad for your crops, so either harvest them before the cold season, or move, either deep underground, or to a place with warmer climate. Most curiously, the planet's trabant seems to complete exactly 12 rotations per solar year, each having 8 days, so if you wanna be accurate, you'll have to rip Hextember from your callendars.

quests.name: Skipping ahead
quests.description: If you're resourceful and smart, you might be able to skip the bloomery entirely. doesn't save you from having to make the bronze anvil though.

tasks.longDescription: You can only claim this reward if you haven't made a bloomery yet. We also need 10 ingots as proof that it wasn't just a fluke or lucky find, but a bit more sustainable.

quests.name: Suiting up
quests.description: Hanai and Snow want to send you to some mildly dangerous places, and i won't stand here and let you die from whatever might lurk there. Go and make some iron or invar armor.

tasks.longDescription: Show me you obtained the following items: *Note: this Quest isn't required to be able to explore those places, just a friendly reminder

quests.name: [i] Swimming and Movement
quests.description: Not everyone wants to carry around a boat all day. fortunately, you are agile enough to swim. simply start sprinting once you're fully submerged in water. Also, sneaking now allows you to get into 1.5-block tall spaces and using things like trapdoors, you can even crawl.

quests.name: Tier 2 smithing
quests.description: To be honest with you, the copper anvil's only purpose is to weld bronze or other tier 2 metal into double ingots for the next anvil.

tasks.longDescription: Show me you have made a Bronze anvil:

quests.name: First Real Tools
quests.description: You might have noticed some nuggets of metal that are mixed in with the rocks. If you found enough copper-rich nuggets on the ground, you can put multiples of 10 into one of your small vessels and place said vessel down on the floor and create another pit kiln. Then, once it is done melting, grab the vessel, click in the air with it, and put in your desired molds to be filled with metal. If you can't find enough copper like that, consider using a goldpan on some gravel and water. If you have enough of some of the trace elements required, you can skip ahead and make alloyed tools right away instead.

tasks.longDescription: A saw and pickaxe are the two most essential tools out of the bunch. Show me that you have made at least those two

quests.name: [i] Sluices
quests.description: Sluices, when provided with water at the top and a place for said water to flow one block below its end, will process any gravel and sand you throw at them and yield you gemstones and, if a metal ore vein is nearby, wash out nuggets of that specific ore. Gravel might become renewable later, so as long as you can set up sluices at the desired location, you can get practically unlimited amounts of any metal ore you like, albeit in nugget form, so not partcularly nice for usage directly in a bloomery or blast furnace.

quests.name: Simple Pipes
quests.description: Fluiducts are a bit difficult to create, but a bronze tube should be perfectly doable. once you have access to iron, you can make fluid hoppers or pumps. Use a wrench to connect/ disconnect pipes.
